full_judgment:
The learned Munsif in his order referred to the case of Shah Wali Vs. Ghulam Din alias Gaman and Mohamad Din, (1967) 19 DLR (S.C.) 143. 

 9. In the instant case, Miscellaneous Case was allowed on 3. 1. 75 with default clause; on that date an order was passed for passing the final order on 18.1.75. As the payment was not made within the time allowed, final order dismissing the Miscellaneous Case with default clause was passed on 18. 1. 75. The very order passed on 3.1.75 with default clause itself was the final order in the case. Moreover, passing of an order on that very date expressly stating that final order would be passed on 18. 1. 75, undoubtedly shows that the Court did not intend to retain any control over the case on passing the final order. The case reported in 27 D.L.R. 232 followed the principle of law laid down in the case reported in 19 D.L.R. (S.C.) 143, that Court has no jurisdiction to make any alteration by extending time limit after it becomes functus afficio. The observation of Mohsen Ali J. in the case reported in 28 D.L.R. 9 quoting from the decision in the case of Malsanath Ram Das Ys. Gana Das reported in A.I.R. 1961, (S.C.) 882 that "It is in my opinion a procedural order though preemptory and in essence, is terrorem so that dilatory litigants might put themselves in order and avoid delay does not appear to be applicable in respect of the order dated 18.1.75 even if it was applicable in respect of the order dated 3.11.75, for, time was allowed under order dated 3.1.75 with default clause, but, the Court also expressed its intention by a separate order to pass the final order subsequently on 18.1.75. Hence after passing of the final order on 18.1.75 the learned Munsif became functus officio. He had no jurisdiction to pass an order on 18.1.75 allowing the extension of time.
